candidate_test_answers.answer: I would use Kadane's algorithm. Maintain the best subarray ending at the current position and the global best. At each element choose between starting a new subarray or extending the current one. This is O(n) time and O(1) extra space. I would initialize from the first element so an all-negative array is handled correctly.

I would check every possible subarray and calculate its sum, keeping the maximum. This is correct but much slower than Kadane's algorithm and can be O(n^2) or O(n^3) depending on how sums are computed.

I would maintain a current sum and maximum sum, adding each value and resetting when the current sum becomes negative. The approach is Kadane's algorithm. I think it is O(n^2) because the maximum is updated repeatedly, with O(1) space.

I would use Kadane's algorithm with a running sum and maximum. If the running sum becomes negative, reset it. This is O(n) time and O(1) space. I would not specifically handle an array where every number is negative.
I would keep adding all values and whenever the sum is negative I reset it. I would return the largest sum I saw, but I am not sure how to initialize it or handle negative-only arrays.
